Interrupt a running check

Source: R/solver.R
z3_interrupt.Rd

Stops the check that is running on solver. It is meant for R code that runs inside that check: the callbacks of a user propagator (z3_propagator()) or of z3_on_clause(), which cannot otherwise use their own solver, and the model callback of an optimizer (z3_on_model()). The check then returns "unknown"; the solver or optimizer stays usable. For a solver z3_reason_unknown() reports "interrupted". An optimizer keeps the best model found so far, whose objective values z3_optimum() reports. Z3 notices the request at its next opportunity, so a callback may still run a few more times. When no check is running, z3_interrupt() does nothing.

Usage

z3_interrupt(solver)

Arguments

solver

A z3_solver or z3_optimize.

Value

solver, invisibly.

Details

Z3 can interrupt a single solver but not a single optimizer; for an optimizer z3_interrupt() interrupts its context while the optimizer's check runs.

Examples

ctx <- z3_context()
if (z3_version_at_least("4.12.3")) {
  p <- z3_bools(ctx, paste0("p", 1:3))
  s <- z3_solver(ctx)
  z3_add(s, z3_or(p), z3_or(!p$p1, !p$p2))
  # Stop the search at the first clause Z3 reports.
  z3_on_clause(s, function(proof_hint, deps, literals) z3_interrupt(s))
  z3_check(s)
}
#> [1] "unknown"

# Stop an optimizer at its first model.
x <- z3_int(ctx, "x")
opt <- z3_optimize(ctx)
z3_add(opt, x >= 0, x <= 100)
obj <- z3_maximize(opt, x)
z3_on_model(opt, function(model) z3_interrupt(opt))
z3_check(opt)
#> [1] "unknown"
z3_optimum(obj)
#> <z3_optimum> 0 (best so far, not proven optimal)
